review_type: AI subagent source review and isolated checker exercises; not human independent review
reviewer_role: Separate review agent for producer/checker. This same agent implemented the pair dependency, so its inspection of that module is not independent authorship review.
status: No blocking soundness issue found in reviewed paths
checks: Fresh selection is all X0/X1 coordinate-anchor triples minus the exact preceding 548-triple union; 132 disjoint complete retained families.
The homology profile contains only the added character and total degrees 3 and 4. Physical pure rows are selected without setting the other coefficients to zero.
For nonempty blocks, exact rational ranks, kernels, boundaries, quotient representatives and d squared zero are reconstructed; a distinct elimination routine checks the first map rank.
Empty blocks contain no homology records and receive score zero by declared convention; this supplies no evidence that a family is easy or its full Koszul complex exact.
Ranking and follow plans are preserved, ties use the predeclared family order, and both comparison groups use the same 120-second continuation method.
Baseline and rebuilt zero coordinates are removed only after explicit square or higher-power rational identities. Shared charts retain the complete stabilizer-allowed numerator correction space.
All expected chart pivots must be present when completed or when removals are applied. A timeout may retain a correct prefix without claiming the untested charts.
Only terminal dependency reduction gives family exclusion; a positive homology score or failed normalized chart does not.
Full X0/X1 pair binding includes all 13 retained directions, checks 11 charts, records 9 failed charts, and invokes the explicit one-character proof only after reduction to X1.

isolated_checker_exercises.method: Copies substituted in memory for one follow packet; no proof or experiment packet changed.

comparison_caveats: High group 19,30,31,49 has added-block variable/generator counts (4,3),(3,4),(3,4),(3,4). Low group 3,16,61,72 has (1,0),(1,0),(3,3),(1,0): the groups are not matched.
Three of the four zero-score controls have no selected pure equations. Depict them separately from nonempty blocks whose H1 vanishes.

The selected pure rows generate a necessary subideal. They are not asserted to exhaust pure-character consequences obtainable by combining mixed rows, so the score is not an intrinsic invariant of the full family.
No randomized or causal efficacy conclusion follows from this small deterministic selection; score separation alone is not demonstrated predictive utility.
Finite Koszul homology is not a full free resolution or an application of the geometric theorems of Yang or the Eisenbud-Erman pairing.
The two physical reconstructions share the identity-replay and finite-complex algorithms. This is not a wholly independently implemented theorem prover or a Lean HasCertificate proof.
